title: The Ungrateful Soldier
author: James Baldwin
summary: 丹麦士兵以德报怨，饶恕了企图杀害他的受伤敌人，因此受封骑士。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1896 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: Here is another story of the battlefield, and it is much like the one which I have just told you.
paragraphs.zh: 下面又是一个战场上的故事，和我刚刚讲过的那个很相似。

paragraphs.en: Not quite a hundred years after the time of Sir Philip Sidney there was a war between the Swedes and the Danes. One day a great battle was fought, and the Swedes were beaten, and driven from the field. A soldier of the Danes who had been slightly wounded was sitting on the ground. He was about to take a drink from a flask. All at once he heard some one say,—
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普·西德尼爵士的时代过去还不到一百年，瑞典人和丹麦人之间爆发了一场战争。一天，双方打了一场大仗，瑞典人战败，被赶出了战场。一名受了轻伤的丹麦士兵坐在地上，正要拿起水壶喝一口。忽然，他听见有人说话：

paragraphs.en: "O sir! give me a drink, for I am dying."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，先生！给我一口水吧，我快死了。”

paragraphs.en: It was a wounded Swede who spoke. He was lying on the ground only a little way off. The Dane went to him at once. He knelt down by the side of his fallen foe, and pressed the flask to his lips.
paragraphs.zh: 说话的是一名受伤的瑞典人。他就躺在不远处的地上。丹麦士兵立刻走过去，在倒下的敌人身边跪下，把水壶送到他唇边。

paragraphs.en: "Drink," said he, "for thy need is greater than mine."

Hardly had he spoken these words, when the Swede raised himself on his elbow. He pulled a pistol from his pocket, and shot at the man who would have befriended him. The bullet grazed the Dane's shoulder, but did not do him much harm.
paragraphs.zh: 话音刚落，那个瑞典人就用胳膊肘撑起身子，从口袋里掏出手枪，向这个本想帮助他的人开枪。子弹擦过丹麦士兵的肩膀，没有造成重伤。

paragraphs.en: "Ah, you rascal!" he cried. "I was going to befriend you, and you repay me by trying to kill me. Now I will punish you. I would have given you all the water, but now you shall have only half." And with that he drank the half of it, and then gave the rest to the Swede.
paragraphs.zh: “啊，你这个恶棍！”他喊道，“我本来想帮你，你却想杀我来报答我。现在我要惩罚你。我本来会把水全都给你，可现在你只能喝一半。”说完，他喝掉一半，把剩下的给了那个瑞典人。

paragraphs.en: When the King of the Danes heard about this, he sent for the soldier and had him tell the story just as it was.
paragraphs.zh: 丹麦国王听说这件事后，召见了这名士兵，让他原原本本地讲了一遍。

paragraphs.en: "Why did you spare the life of the Swede after he had tried to kill you?" asked the king.
paragraphs.zh: “他试图杀你，你为什么还饶他一命？”国王问。

paragraphs.en: "Because, sir," said the soldier, "I could never kill a wounded enemy."
paragraphs.zh: “因为，陛下，”士兵说，“我绝不会杀死一个受伤的敌人。”

paragraphs.en: "Then you deserve to be a nobleman," said the king. And he rewarded him by making him a knight, and giving him a noble title.
paragraphs.zh: “那么你配得上做一个高尚的人。”国王说。他授予这名士兵骑士身份和贵族头衔，以此奖赏他。
